slot.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slot.brief: Regular polygonal current loop (e.g., square or hexagon) or a two-wire setup; superpose fields from the sides/wires at the centre and find the net magnetic field, possibly using a stated limiting-case check.

stem: A square loop of side $0.40\ \text{m}$ carries a current of $5.0\ \text{A}$. Find the magnitude of the magnetic field at its centre. Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \text{T m A}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: Each side contributes \(B_1=\frac{\mu_0 I\sqrt{2}}{2\pi a}\) at the centre. Thus \(B=4B_1=\frac{2\mu_0 I\sqrt{2}}{\pi a}=1.0\times10^{-5}\sqrt{2}\,\text{T}\).

working:
$B=4\left[\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi(a/2)}(2\sin45^\circ)\right]=\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}\mu_0 I}{\pi a}=1.0\times10^{-5}\sqrt{2}\ \text{T}$

Independent check: Each side contributes \(B_1=\frac{\mu_0 I\sqrt{2}}{2\pi a}\) at the centre. Thus \(B=4B_1=\frac{2\mu_0 I\sqrt{2}}{\pi a}=1.0\times10^{-5}\sqrt{2}\,\text{T}\).
solution:
The field due to a finite straight wire is $B_1=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}(\sin\theta_1+\sin\theta_2)$. Here $r=a/2$ and $\theta_1=\theta_2=45^\circ$, so
$$B=4B_1=\frac{2\sqrt{2}\mu_0 I}{\pi a}=1.0\times10^{-5}\sqrt{2}\ \text{T}.$$
